cohort: 185 women delivering healthy term newborns who were placed in skin-to-skin contact within sixty minutes after birth.
finding: Mothers admitted for planned cesarean deliveries were less likely to intend to breastfeed than those expecting vaginal deliveries, and among mothers intending to breastfeed, longer initial breastfeeding sessions were associated with higher rates of exclusive breastfeeding before hospital discharge.
mod_finding: Mothers planning a cesarean delivery were significantly less likely to intend to breastfeed compared to those expecting a vaginal delivery.
